facts.statement: The species Hesperonychus elizabethae was named in honor of Dr. Elizabeth Nicholls, who collected the fossils as a student in 1982.
facts.quote: The type species was named in honor of Dr. Elizabeth Nicholls of the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology who collected it as a student in 1982.

facts.statement: Hesperonychus lived around 75 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: It is known from fossils recovered from the Dinosaur Park Formation and possibly from the uppermost strata of the Oldman Formation of Alberta, dating to the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous around 75 million years ago.

facts.statement: The primary fossil evidence for Hesperonychus is a partial pelvic girdle known as holotype specimen UALVP 48778.
facts.quote: Hesperonychus is mainly known from one partial pelvic girdle, holotype specimen UALVP 48778, collected by Dr. Elizabeth Nicholls in Dinosaur Provincial Park in 1982.

facts.statement: The gracile appearance of associated toe bones suggests Hesperonychus likely did not belong to the Eudromaeosauria.
facts.quote: The gracile appearances of these potential toe bones make it unlikely that Hesperonychus belonged to the Eudromaeosauria.

facts.statement: The fused pubic bones indicate that the Hesperonychus specimen represents an adult dinosaur rather than a juvenile.
facts.quote: the pubic bones were fused, a characteristic of adult dinosaurs, indicating that the specimen does not represent a juvenile of a known species.

facts.statement: Longrich and Currie classified Hesperonychus as a member of the Microraptorinae, a group previously thought to be restricted to the Early Cretaceous of Asia.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Longrich and Currie found Hesperonychus to be a member of the Microraptorinae, a clade of small dromaeosaurids previously thought to be restricted to the Early Cretaceous of Asia.

facts.statement: In 2012, Martyniuk classified Hesperonychus as a eudromaeosaurian.
facts.quote: In 2012, Martyniuk considered Hesperonychus as a eudromaeosaurian.

facts.statement: In 2019, Hartman and colleagues suggested Hesperonychus was an avialan close to modern birds, though they disagreed with the classification of microraptorines as avialans.
facts.quote: In 2019, Hartman and colleagues suggested that Hesperonychus is actually an avialan close to modern birds like Balaur bondoc based on phylogenetic analyses, though they disagreed with microraptorines being avialans.

facts.statement: In 2020, Hesperonychus was recovered as a dromaeosaurid that was a sister taxon to, but not a member of, the microraptorines.
facts.quote: In 2020, Hesperonychus was recovered as a dromaeosaurid and a sister taxon, but not a member, of the polytomic microraptorines.

facts.statement: In 2014, Brusatte and colleagues excluded Hesperonychus from phylogenetic analyses due to a lack of data, indicating its classification remains uncertain.
facts.quote: In 2014, Brusatte and colleagues pruned five "wildcard" taxa including the paravians Pyroraptor and Hesperonychus from phylogenetic analyses, mainly due to a huge lack of data, indicating that the definitive classifications of these taxa are uncertain.

facts.statement: Hesperonychus was assigned to Microraptoria based on features including a spatulate pubic symphysis, a curved pubic shaft, and lateral tubercules expanded into wing-like structures.
facts.quote: Hesperonychus was assigned to Microraptoria due to having a spatulate (rounded) pubic symphysis, a strong posterior curvature of the distal shaft of the pubis, and lateral tubercules on the pubes, which are expanded into 'wing-like' structures in the case of Hesperonychus.

facts.statement: Longrich and Currie concluded Hesperonychus likely did not have four wings or glide like Microraptor, but was more similar in behavior to Sinornithosaurus.
facts.quote: Longrich and Currie concluded that it was unlikely for Hesperonychus to exhibit four wings or gliding behavior as in Microraptor, and speculated that it was more likely to be similar to Sinornithosaurus given their closer similarity in size.

facts.statement: Hesperonychus appears to have been a common feature of the Dinosaur Park Formation environment, with at least ten distinct specimens found compared to fewer remains of other small carnivores.
facts.quote: Hesperonychus helped to fill that gap, especially since, given the number of fragmentary remains and claws that have been collected (representing at least ten distinct specimens, compared to thirty of the contemporary Saurornitholestes and two of Dromaeosaurus), it appears to have been a very common feature of the Dinosaur Park Formation environment.

facts.statement: Hesperonychus is the smallest known non-avian carnivorous dinosaur from North America.
facts.quote: Es el dinosaurio carnívoro no aviano más pequeño conocido de Norteamérica

facts.statement: Hesperonychus lived approximately 75 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió en el período Cretácico Superior, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The species Hesperonychus elizabethae was described by Nicholas R. Longrich and Philip J. Currie in 2009 and is the only species in the genus.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Hesperonychus elizabethae, fue descrita por Nicholas R. Longrich y Philip J. Currie en 2009 y es la única especie asignada al género.

facts.statement: Hesperonychus fossils were found in the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Hesperonychus se realizó en los estratos de la Formación Dinosaur Park, en Alberta (Canadá).

facts.statement: It was the first small carnivorous theropod found at the site, weighing less than 10 kg, and the first microraptor described in North America.
facts.quote: Fue la primera vez que se encontró en este yacimiento un terópodo carnívoro pequeño, de menos de 10 kg, así como la primera vez que se describe un microrráptor en Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The species was named in honor of Elizabeth Nicholls, the woman who found the specimen in 1982.
facts.quote: La especie tipo fue nombrada en honor a la mujer que lo encontró en 1982, Elizabeth Nicholls.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UALVP 48778 is a partial pelvic girdle collected by Dr. Elizabeth Nicholls in 1982.
facts.quote: Hesperonychus se conoce de un cintura pélvica parcial, el espécimen holotipo UALVP 48778, recogido por el Dr. Elizabeth Nicholls en el parque provincial del dinosaurio en 1982.

facts.statement: A series of very small toe bones, including sickle claws, in the Royal Tyrrell Museum collection may also belong to Hesperonychus.
facts.quote: Una serie de huesos muy pequeños del dedo del pie, incluidas las "garras de la hoz", en la colección del Museo Royal Tyrrell también pueden pertenecer a Hesperonychus.

facts.statement: Despite its small size, the fused pubic bones indicate the specimen is an adult and not a juvenile of a known species.
facts.quote: A pesar de su pequeño tamaño, los huesos púbicos se fusionaron, una característica de los dinosaurios adultos, lo que indica que el espécimen no representa un juvenil de una especie conocida.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Hesperonychus in Microraptorinae, a clade of small dromaeosaurids previously restricted to Early Cretaceous Asia.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético realizado por Longrich y Currie encuentra a Hesperonychus para ser miembro de Microraptorinae, un clado de pequeños dromeosáuridos que previamente se encontraban restringidos al Cretácico Inferior de Asia.

facts.statement: The discovery of Hesperonychus in the Late Cretaceous Campanian extends the fossil range of microraptorines by 45 million years compared to the previously known Late Aptian Microraptor.
facts.quote: El más joven microrraptorino previamente conocido era el Microraptor proveniente de estratos del Aptiense a mediados del Cretácico, pero el descubrimiento del Hesperonychus en el Campaniense del finales del Cretácico agranda el rango fósil de los microraptorinos 45 millones de años.

facts.statement: Hesperonychus was assigned to Microraptoria due to features like a spatulate, rounded pubic symphysis and lateral tubercles that expand into wing-like structures.
facts.quote: Hesperonychus se asignó a Microraptoria debido a que tenía una sínfisis púbica espatulada, redondeada, una fuerte curvatura posterior del eje distal del pubis y tubérculos laterales en los pubis, que se expanden en estructuras en forma de ala en el caso de Hesperonychus.

facts.statement: Hesperonychus was likely very common in the Dinosaur Park Formation environment, with at least ten distinct specimens found compared to thirty Saurornitholestes and two Dromaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Hesperonychus ayudó a llenar ese hueco, especialmente puesto que, dado el número de restos y de garras fragmentarias que se han recogido que representan por lo menos diez especímenes distintos, comparados a treinta del contemporáneo Saurornitholestes y dos de Dromaeosaurus, aparece haber sido una característica muy común del ambiente la formación Dinosaur Park.

facts.statement: It is debated whether dinosaur competition prevented mammals from growing larger, if mammal competition allowed dinosaurs to remain tiny, or if both factors were at play.
facts.quote: Longrich & Currie que cualquier competición de dinosaurios impidió a los mamíferos un crecimiento más grande, la opinión tradicional, o que la competición con los mamíferos no dejó a los dinosaurios tener un tamaño minúsculo, o ambas posiciones a la vez.

facts.statement: The parent group of Hesperonychus is Microraptorinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Microraptorinae

facts.statement: Hesperonychus belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Hesperonychus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Hesperonychus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
